cohort: 6234 women at ≥ 37 weeks' gestation who were monitored during the last 4 hours of tracings before birth in an academic community hospital
finding: Uterine tachysystole (UT) was common (18.3%) but usually benign, and while not associated with neonatal depression or metabolic acidemia, these babies often showed decelerations at contraction rates below UT levels.
